This Miscellaneous First Appeal Is Filed U/S
173(1) Of Mv Act Against The Judgment And Award
Dated 01.4.2011 Passed In Mvc No.83/2007 On The File
Of The Senior Civil Judge And Mact, Malavalli,
Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT
Though the matter is listed for orders, but with the consent of both the learned counsels appearing for the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant for seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC.No.83/2007 dated 01.04.2011 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Malavalli (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal').
NC: 2024:KHC:45671 3.
The factum of accident, injuries sustained by the appellant/claimant are not in dispute.
4. For the sake of convenience and easy reference, the parties are referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.

5. Heard the arguments addressed by both the learned counsels appearing for the parties and perused the materials placed on record.
6.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the various heads as follows:

Sl. Particulars Amount in Rs.
No.
 1. Towards injury, pain and suffering 30,000/-
 2. Towards Medical and Hospital charges 18,500/-
 3. Towards Attendant charges 20,000/-
 4. Towards Discomfort in life 10,000/-

From the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the appellant/claimant has suffered the following injuries:
i. Abrasion over the left face.
NC: 2024:KHC:45671
ii. Injury to lower abdomen.
iii. Scrotal adema.

iv. Fracture of patella region etc.,
8.
As per the doctors evidence, injury No.3 is grievous in nature.
The appellant/claimant being a minor boy of 8 year old has suffered the above stated injuries.
The doctor is examined as PW-2 and according to him, the minor boy has suffered 25% of permanent physical disability towards whole body and disability to the particular part
is not forthcoming in the evidence of PW-2.
But considering the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant/claimant, the appellant/claimant is finding difficulty in the urinating process.
Therefore, from the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and significant disability to the sensitive part of the body.
9. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.18,500/- under the head medical expenses, which is as per the medical bills produced and it is found to be just and proper.
Hence, it is kept intact.
The appellant/claimant is a minor boy of 8 years old at the time of accident.

Therefore, in the case of injuries sustained by minor children what would be the compensation to be awarded is guided by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun vs.
Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd.,1.

Thus, the appellant/claimant is entitled to compensation under various heads as follows:
 HEAD COMPENSATION  AMOUNT  Pain and suffering already Rs.3,00,000/-
 undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability Discomfort, inconvenience and loss Rs.25,000/- of earnings to the parents during the period of Mahesh Kumar vs M Mahadevu on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148216436/
3 hospitalization Medical expenses Rs.18,500/-
Future medical expenses for Rs.25,000/- correction of the mal union of fracture and incidental expenses for such treatment TOTAL Rs.3,68,500/-
|
11.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.78,500/-.
But the appellant/claimant is entitled for AIR 2014 SC 736 NC: 2024:KHC:45671 total compensation of Rs.3,68,500/-.

entities.text: AIR 2014 SC 736 NC: 2024:KHC:45671 total compensation of Rs.3,68,500/-.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,90,000/- (Rs.3,68,500/- -
Rs.78,500/-) along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
12.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. The Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii.
The impugned judgment and award dated 01.04.2011 passed in MVC No.83/2007 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Malavalli, is hereby modified.

iii. The appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,90,000/- (Rs.3,68,500/- -
Rs.78,500/-) along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iv. No order as to costs.
NC: 2024:KHC:45671 v.
The appellant/claimant is not entitled to interest for the delay period of 225 days in filing the appeal.

vi. Draw award accordingly.
